summary:
Reviewed frozen HEAD **`01697be71f6d1ddfbc11bf56a42dd966fa54291b`**, with change range **`826f142045d1d3b23c6398116defc2b39522a5d0..01697be71f6d1ddfbc11bf56a42dd966fa54291b`**. The worktree remained clean. This was source/evidence inspection only; I ran no builds, tests, GPU work, apps, or agents.

**A bounded no-op-on-withdrawal policy is warranted for supplemental regional admission.** The latest margin fix closes Opus’s concrete r9 examples, but does not establish that an owned line was completely observed.

1. **Medium: an optional region can still delete confirmed words and cause recurring flicker.**

   The [ownership check](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:3108) uses the previous detector union. It cannot bound the next detector’s jitter.

   Concrete source-level trace: use ROI `[0,400) × [0,200)`. An accepted “end here” line has its last detector box ending at `x=390`, so it satisfies the ten-pixel ownership margin. Crop detection shifts that edge three pixels to `393`. The [backend’s eight-pixel exclusion](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/uct_paddle_processing.cpp:238) drops “here”. Admission sees only the complete, interior “end” candidate; the rejected-candidate guard cannot see a word already removed by the backend. The replacement overlaps the old line, defeating omission retention, and [the old owned line is discarded](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:3507).

   “Here” disappears from enhanced text and reading output without an omission marker. Even a successful current probe does not prevent this partial replacement. The three-pixel change is within the owner’s exploratory geometry tolerance; that tolerance does not justify losing the word.

   Contained spelling disagreement follows the same withdrawal path: confirmed “itself” → regional “itelf” becomes pending and masks the word. Pending demand triggers full OCR; two agreeing full observations can restore it, after which another region can repeat the cycle. This is reachable policy behavior, not evidence that either spelling is accurate.

   **Bounded repair:** preflight the complete proposed regional update and reject it atomically if it would withdraw an existing owned word. Match exact text one-to-one, preserving multiplicity and order with the established geometry rules. Include withdrawals caused by protection/cap handling. A refused update must leave IDs, masks, pending tickets and proof clocks unchanged, without creating pending/full-demand work merely from optional disagreement. Keep the one-attempt interval limit.

   Full scans and independent probes retain authority. Never restore a probe-invalidated line or extend freshness. This deliberately postpones a potentially correct regional correction until authoritative work resolves it; it does not loosen recognition agreement or declare old text correct.

2. **Medium: immutable refinement can lose newly discovered protection when every safe word is appended or deduplicated.**

   In the [immutable merge](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:2951), appending a proved word to an existing reading line clears its `keep` entry. If no words remain, line 2988 skips the candidate entirely. Its `protectedSceneRects` and `nonCarvableSceneRects` are not transferred.

   Concrete trace: an old line contains two confirmed words with a gap between them. Detail finds a new, independently corroborated word in that gap and a nearby rejected operator. The new word is appended to the old line; the operator exists only in the candidate’s protection lists. No fragment remains, so those lists disappear. The newly drawn word’s padded plate can cover the operator that the detail result explicitly required protecting.

   Duplicate-only candidates have the same loss. This is a **pre-existing gap in the touched merge**, also noted in r8; adding non-carvable classification does not close it.

   **Bounded repair:** preserve incoming protection independently of whether a candidate contributes a remaining word fragment. Apply the existing total mask limit and keep semantic-risk/invalid-geometry protection non-carvable. Avoid suppressing unrelated proved words unnecessarily.

3. **Medium: quad-aware proof is still converted to a rectangular carving footprint.**

   The [carving operation](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:2841) subtracts rectangles. `provedFootprints` receives `sceneRect`, including for tilted words whose actual displayed geometry is a quad. The new cross-line pass extends this subtraction to other retained lines.

   A concrete geometric counterexample is the quad `(100,100), (140,140), (120,160), (80,120)`. Its bounding rectangle contains a small punctuation mask around `(115,156)`, although that mask lies outside the proved quad. Rectangular subtraction removes the mask. The painter’s [six-percent vertical plate padding](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/ui/ultra_clear_text_overlay.cpp:553) extends into that area and can cover the punctuation.

   Ordinary low-confidence/too-small punctuation is carvable, so the semantic-risk guard does not prevent this. This is a source-derived geometry counterexample, not a newly rendered reproduction.

   **Bounded repair:** retain the quad in the carving descriptor. Subtract its shape conservatively within the existing cap, or refuse ambiguous cuts that would uncover protection outside the quad. Increasing margins or globally clamping typography would not address the proof mismatch.

4. **Medium, diagnostic: a regional withdrawal can publish a new revision attributed to the previous OCR job.**

   [Admission can return `kPending`](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:3574) after replacing an owned word with uncertainty while retaining another pane’s accepted text. [NoteTimingAdmission](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/app/ultra_clear_text_controller.cpp:1857) ignores non-immutable `kPending` and `kEmpty`, leaving the previous admission ticket cached.

   `RefreshOverlay` then observes changed positioned content and allocates a new publication revision using that old ticket. Thus the revision is new, but its causal OCR identity is wrong. Successful regional updates retaining outside proof also do not explicitly mark that mixed provenance as `RetainedArtifact`.

   **Bounded repair:** distinguish “model changed” from “new glyph accepted” and “optional no-op”. Attribute actual mutations to their result, mark retained mixed proof, and leave no-op/pan tickets unchanged.

   This concerns diagnostic publication attribution; it is not evidence that NVDA speaks stale text.

5. **Low–medium: replacing a queued region can leave `regionalJob_` permanently occupied.**

   A valid scheduling interleaving remains:

   - The idle worker receives region R, but has not dequeued it.
   - A later CPU probe creates full demand.
   - The controller’s `regionalJob_` allowance permits full F to replace R.
   - [Enqueue drops the coalesced descriptor](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/common/ultra_clear_text.cpp:1830) without a completion.
   - F completes, but only a regional completion or invalidation clears `regionalJob_`.

   Subsequent optional submissions require `!regionalJob_`, so regions remain disabled until invalidation. Full scans continue. The scheduling window is uncommon, but no synchronization excludes it; this is stronger than an impossible-state conjecture, though I did not reproduce it.

   **Bounded repair:** explicitly retire the controller’s regional ticket when a successful full submission supersedes it, rejecting any later obsolete regional completion, or report exact superseded-job identity from enqueue.

6. **Low: original one-axis subpixel masks can protect nothing.**

   [ProtectedRegion](Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-9418ce98/src/ui/ultra_clear_text_overlay.cpp:58) cannot distinguish a carved remainder from an original mask. For example, `[100.1,100.35) × [100,115)` contains no horizontal pixel centre but many vertical centres; it becomes an empty region. Nearby plate padding can cover that original thin mark.

   The r6 strip repair correctly prevents carved slivers from suppressing adjacent words. A possible bounded follow-up is to distinguish original protection from subtraction remainders, rather than restoring outward rounding universally. The separate approximately half-view-pixel edge approximation remains a small rendering limitation.

The **revised timing fixture is meaningful**. It directly compares complete consumer tickets, requires an actual later paint, checks painted revision and accessibility publication count, and retains the negative-event assertions only for a lossless snapshot. Requiring `coverageIncomplete` and serialized latency ineligibility on loss is appropriate. I found no reason to block the recorder or retry contention. Finding 4 is a different admission case that this pane-only fixture does not exercise.

The r8 crossing/outside-line and mask-remainder repairs look sound by inspection. The r9 detector-union guard and whole-admission rejection address their specified examples. Per-observation pending tickets retain acquisition identity; regional outputs do not update planner observations. I found no new ownership defect in the changed resident-input or supplemental automatic-backend paths. This is not a fresh audit of the entire CUDA implementation.

Several pieces are worth simplifying, as follow-up work only:

- **Remove optional-to-full fallback where possible.** Yielding unusable regional descriptors to ordinary full scheduling would reduce mixed result states and accounting branches.
- **Make regional admission one bounded transaction.** Complete-line ownership plus withdrawal preflight is simpler than iterative ownership closure or word-level reconstruction.
- **Separate execution descriptors from shadow diagnostics.** Active selection mainly consumes geometry and identity; hypothetical occurrence/debt statistics must not be interpreted as regions actually executed. Full scans currently provide coverage.
- **Centralize word conversion and mask transfer.** Repeated aggregate conversions already caused metadata omissions. Explicit helpers would reduce that maintenance risk.
- **Keep typography identity separate from reading identity.** `layoutGroupId` serves a concrete purpose; deleting it would reintroduce unrelated font/baseline coupling.

The saved book evidence still leaves quality objections open: the reported wide 6× “to” fit and weak foreground estimate are plausible fit/color problems, while outputs such as “itelf” and “ante” are model-recognition limitations. The approximately 2.2-source-pixel detector-edge overrun does **not** establish a violation of the ten-pixel exploratory allowance. Neither higher painted-word counts nor unchanged raw OCR establishes accuracy. I would not prescribe a global type clamp from this evidence.

I read repository `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, the required developer/index/path/license documentation, relevant code-reference and UCT regional/planner/immutable/geometry/timing documents, the changed UCT implementation and surrounding admission/publication paths, relevant fixtures, saved Opus r6/r8/r9 reports, and selected book/GPU/compile receipts. Video and the precision experiment were outside this review.

At `01697be`, the saved receipt establishes CPU target compilation; your update adds shipping-app compilation. **Latest tests remain queued.** Earlier scoped passes and the scheduler-only GPU proof do not establish current regional text-admission acceptance. The original timing failure remains retained pending the repaired fixture’s run. Native desktop, NVDA, camera, audible-device and complete release acceptance remain open; this review supplies no latency, 120 FPS, or RTX 3050 claim.
